questions.q: There are& $m$~men and two women participating in a chess tournament. Each participant plays two games with every other participant. If the number of games played by the men between themselves exceeds the number of games played between the men and the women by~$84$, then the value of~$m$& is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, number of men is& $m$~and number of women is~$2 .$

Since each participants competes two games~with each other, Hence count of men Vs men total number of game plays $= 2{ }^{m}{C}_{2}$.

count of men Vs women~total number of game~plays $= 4m$.

As per given condition in question,

$2{ }^{m}{C}_{2} = 84 + 4m$

$⇒ m^{2} - 5m - 84 = 0$

$⇒ m^{2} - 12m + 7m - 84 = 0$

$⇒ \left(m - 12\right)\left(m + 7\right) = 0$.

$⇒ m = 12, - 7$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The word 'MATHEMATICS' consists of $11$ letters including two $M ' s$, two $T ' s$ and two~$A ' s$,

Now, first we will arrange letters~_M_A_T_H_E_M_A_T_I_.

Here, we have~$10$~gaps to fill~$C \text{ and } S$.

The number of words with or without meaning can be formed from the word~$MATHEMATICS$~when~$C, S$~does not come together is

$= \dfrac{9 !}{2 ! \cdot 2 ! \cdot 2 !} \times C2 10 \times 2 !$

$= \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 !}{2 ! \cdot 2 !} \times \dfrac{10 \times 9}{2}$

$= 5670$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Consider a rectangle $ABCD$~having $5, 6, 7, 9$ points in the interior of the line segments $AB, BC, CD, DA$ respectively. Then~  \left(\beta - \alpha\right)$ is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\alpha =$ Number of triangles

$\alpha = 5 \cdot 6 \cdot 7 + 5 \cdot 7 \cdot 9 + 5 \cdot 6 \cdot 9 + 6 \cdot 7 \cdot 9$

$= 210 + 315 + 270 + 378$

$= 1173$

$\beta =$ Number of Quadrilateral

$\beta = 5 \cdot 6 \cdot 7 \cdot 9 = 1890$

$\beta - \alpha = 1890 - 1173 = 717$

questions.q: The number of numbers, strictly between $5000$ and $10000$ can be formed using the digits $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$ without repetition, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Numbers& $1, 3, 5, 7, 9$

Now to form number between~$5000 - 10000$

$\begin{cases}\mathop{_ ⏟}_{5, 7, 9} & \mathop{_ ⏟}_{4\text{ways}} & \mathop{_ ⏟}_{3\text{ways}} & \mathop{_ ⏟}_{2\text{ways}}\end{cases}$

Here at~$1000 ' \text{s}$~place should be taken by~$5, 7 \text{ and } 9$

So for~$1000 ' \text{s}$~place there will be~$3$~ways,

Now for hundredth place there will be~$4$~ways,

For ten's place there will be~$3$~ways,

And for unit place there will be~$2$~ways,

So total ways will be~$3 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 72$& ways.

$G, H, O, T, U$

$= 4 ! = 24$

Number of words starting with~$H$

$= 4 ! = 24$

$= 4 ! = 24$

questions.q: The number of ways of selecting two numbers& $a$ and~$b$, $a \in \left\{2, 4, 6, \ldots \ldots , 100\right\}$ and $b \in \left\{1, 3, 5, \ldots \ldots , 99\right\}$ such that $2$ is the remainder when $a + b$ is divided by $23$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $a = \left\{2, 4, 6, . . . , 100\right\}$~and~$b = \left\{1, 3, 5, . . . , 99\right\}$

Let

$a + b = 23\lambda + 2$

If~$\lambda = 1$, then

$a + b = 25$

So,~\left\{\left(1, 24\right), \left(3, 22\right), . . . . , \left(23, 2\right)\right\}$

Total ordered pairs$= 12$

If~$\lambda = 2$, then

$a + b = 48$

No ordered pair possible.

If~$\lambda = 3$, then

$a + b = 71$

So,

\left\{\left(1, 70\right), \left(3, 68\right), \left(5, 66\right), . . . . , \left(61, 10\right), \left(63, 8\right), \left(65, 6\right), \left(67, 4\right), \left(69, 2\right)\right\}$

Total~$35$~ordered pairs.

If~$\lambda = 5$, then

$a + b = 117$

\left\{\left(17, 100\right), \left(19, 98\right), . . . , \left(99, 18\right)\right\}$

Total~$42$~ordered pairs.

If~$\lambda = 7$, then

$a + b = 163$

So,

\left\{\left(63, 100\right), \left(65, 63\right), . . . . \left(99, 64\right)\right\}$

Total~$19$~pairs.

No further case possible.

So,~required number is

$= 12 + 35 + 42 + 19 = 108$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We need to find the number of& $5$~digit numbers greater than~$40000$~and divisible by~$5$.

Case I : Numbers~start with $5$.

Here if the number starts with~$5$~it should end with~$0$~to be divisible by~$5$.

Case III : The number starts with~$9$~and the last digit should have~$0$~or~$5$.

Total numbers $= 120$.

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: The number of seven digits odd numbers, that can be formed using all the seven digits $1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
To find the number of& $7$~digit odd number formed by using the seven digits~$1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5$

We will take following cases,

Case~$1 -$~fixing~$1$~as unit place,

So total number of ways will be~$\dfrac{6 !}{3 ! 2 !}\left\{\text{as}2\text{is repeating three times and 3 is repeating two times}\right\}$

Case~$2 -$~fixing~$3$~unit place,

So total number of ways will be~$\dfrac{6 !}{3 !}$

Case~$3 -$~fixing~$5$~as unit place,

So total number of ways will be~$\dfrac{6 !}{3 ! 2 !}$

Now adding all the cases we will get, total number of ways as~$\dfrac{6 !}{3 ! 2 !} + \dfrac{6 !}{3 !} + \dfrac{6 !}{3 ! 2 !} = 60 + 120 + 60 = 240$

questions.q: A class contains $b$~boys and $g$ girls. If the number of ways of selecting $3$ boys and $2$ girls from the class is $168$, then $b + 3g$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $b\text{boys and g girls}$

Also given total ways of selecting $3\text{boys and 2 girls}$~which will be~$C3 b \times C2 g = 168$

$⇒ \dfrac{b\left(b - 1\right)\left(b - 2\right)}{6} \times \dfrac{g\left(g - 1\right)}{2} = 168$

$⇒ b\left(b - 1\right)\left(b - 2\right)g\left(g - 1\right) = 7 \times 6 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 2$

$⇒ b\left(b - 1\right)\left(b - 2\right)g\left(g - 1\right) = 8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 3 \times 2$

Now on comparing both side we get,~$b = 8$~and~$g = 3 ⇒ b + 3g = 8 + 9 = 17$

The lines ${L}_{1}, {L}_{2}, . .. , {L}_{20}$ are distinct. For $n = 1, 2, 3, . .. , 10$ all the lines ${L}_{2n - 1}$ are parallel to each other and all the lines ${L}_{2n}$ pass through a given point $P$. The maximum number of points of intersection of pairs of lines from the set \left\{{L}_{1}, {L}_{2}, . .. , {L}_{20}\right\}$ is equal to:

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

Out of $20$ numbered lines, even numbered lines are concurrent, odd number lines are parallel.

So, the maximum number of intersection points will be given by,

$N = \left(1 \to \text{point of intersection when both lines are even}\right) + \left(0 \to \text{point of intersection when both lines are parallel}\right) + \left($C1 10 $\times$C1 10 \to $\text{point of intersection when}$1$\text{odd and}$1$\text{even line meets}\right)

$⇒ N = 1 + 0 + 100$

$⇒ N = 101$

$

questions.q: The number of words, with or without meaning, that can be formed by taking 4 letters at a time from the letters of the word 'SYLLABUS' such that two letters are distinct and two letters are alike, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
From the given word,& $S - 2, L - 2, A, B, Y, U$.

Number of alike letter pairs~$= 2$

Number of ways to select one pair$= C1 2$

Number of distinct letters$= 5$

Number of ways to select two distinct letters$= C2 5$

Number of ways to arrange four letters~if~two are alike$= \dfrac{4 !}{2 !}$

Required number of ways~$= C1 2 C2 5 \cdot \dfrac{4 !}{2 !} = 2 \cdot 10 \cdot \dfrac{24}{2} = 240$
